extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of social/economic theory (sociology, anthropology, political economy); readers of Veblen
extracted.subtask_description: Identify and evaluate the economic and social character of devout observances, sacerdotal life, and related consumption/leisures in a modern industrial community. The page frames these phenomena as economically meaningful traits (conspicuous waste, vicarious leisure, status-signalling) and traces class and gender patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conspicuous waste (devout consumption)
rubrics_metrics.description: The consumption of ceremonial paraphernalia required by any cult (shrines, temples, churches, vestments, sacrifices, sacraments, holiday attire, etc.) serves no immediate material end and may be broadly characterized as items of conspicuous waste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes priestly education, priestly service, pilgrimages, fasts, holidays, household devotions; such consumption extends and protracts the vogue of habits of thought characteristic of the regime of status and, directly and indirectly, curtails the community's economic efficiency by lowering communal vitality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vicarious leisure / sacred holidays as a tithe
rubrics_metrics.description: Sacred holidays are to be construed as a season of vicarious leisure performed for the divinity or saint in whose name the tabu is imposed, i.e., a tithe of vicarious leisure levied on the body of the people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characteristic features include a rigid tabu on all activity of human use during the holiday and, in fast-days, compulsory abstention from consumption that conduces to comfort; secular holidays shade off from sacred ones (example: Labor Day).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priestly abstention from productive work
rubrics_metrics.description: The priest should not put his hand to mechanically productive work; the tabu for the priestly class includes an injunction against seeking worldly gain even where it may be had without debasing application to industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeking material gain as a clergyman is felt to be unworthy and contemptible; the ideal sacerdotal office requires avoidance of economic activity that would suggest attention to temporal welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priestly consumption must be vicarious, not for personal comfort
rubrics_metrics.description: Clerical consumption should take forms that do not obviously conduce to the priest's own comfort or fullness of life and should conform to rules governing vicarious consumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include mortification of the flesh; priests should not appear well fed or in high spirits; ostentatious personal enjoyment or levity jars on sensibilities and is seen as improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priestly diction and homiletical decorum (aloofness from trade/industry)
rubrics_metrics.description: The diction proper to the sanctuary and to the priestly office should carry little if any suggestion of effective everyday life and should not draw upon the vocabulary of modern trade or industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clergy should avoid detailed or intimate handling of industrial/temporal questions; secular matters should be handled with a degree of generality and aloofness implying representation of a master whose interest in secular affairs is permissive and limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ceremonial 'cleanness' and archaic apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: Devout edifices and priestly/court apparatus are invariably of an archaic cast; garments of attendants must be special, ornate, and in some degree archaic, carrying as little suggestion as may be of any industrial occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ceremonial cleanness extends to apparel and, to a lesser degree, to food consumed on sacred holidays; attire should avoid traces of industry and should exhibit conspicuous waste as status-signalling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gambling practices under clerical sanction foster animistic habit
rubrics_metrics.description: Gambling practices such as the church bazaar or raffle recruit and conserve the animistic habit of mind and are legitimized to varying degrees in connection with devout observances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such trivial opportunities for gambling appeal more to devout members of religious organizations than to less devout persons and parallel the proclivity toward sports and appeal to luck.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devout observances as index of predatory/status temperament
rubrics_metrics.description: Devout observances indicate a concomitant variation of temperament accompanying the predatory habit of mind and are an index of habits (sense of personal dignity, invidious comparison, allegiance/subservience) that are industrially disserviceable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The anthropomorphic cults and propitiatory observances appeal to a sense of status (fealty, precedence); such sentiments obstruct organization of industry under modern conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devoutness as atavistic/survival trait relative to industrial life
rubrics_metrics.description: Viewed from the industrial point of view, devoutness is to be looked upon as a survival from an earlier phase of associated life—a mark of arrested spiritual development; exceptional devoutness is an atavistic trait.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modern industrial life favors a matter-of-fact temper that recognizes quantitative, dispassionate force and sequence; devout habits hinder adaptation to this regime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class distribution: leisure and indigent classes more devout
rubrics_metrics.description: Devoutness survives in greater vigor among classes that do not primarily enter the industrial process: (1) the leisure class proper (shielded from economic pressure), and (2) indigent classes (unduly exposed to stress, lack opportunity to adapt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artisan and middle classes (effective industrial community) tend toward secularization; where leisure and indigent classes preponderate, popular sentiment and community devoutness persist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-conforming sects represent partial/half-caste priesthood
rubrics_metrics.description: Clergy of denominations that have diverged from traditional sacerdotal usage often exhibit imperfect conformity to the sacerdotal scheme and are a 'half-caste priesthood' blending sacerdotal traits with alien motives (humanitarian, philanthropic, conviviality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such sects vary in degree of conformity; over generations a spokesman may re-specialize into a full priesthood with austere, archaic, vicarious manners as organizations gain wealth and reassert sacerdotal proprieties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supernatural hierarchy and status-driven vicarious consumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond the priestly class lies a superhuman vicarious leisure class (saints, angels, etc.) organized by status; the good fame of these orders commonly requires tribute in the form of vicarious consumption and leisure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many cults devote sub-orders of attendants/dependents who perform vicarious leisure on behalf of these supernatural ranks, mirroring secular status hierarchies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devout consumption parallels chieftain/court conspicuous waste
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a striking parallelism between consumption for an anthropomorphic divinity and that for a gentleman of leisure (chieftain/patriarch): expensive edifices, archaic fittings, ornate servants' apparel, and conspicuous waste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both forms of consumption serve to enhance prestige and good repute; sacerdotal apparatus is typically more archaic and ritualized than secular court display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priestly avoidance of levity and avowed ambition
rubrics_metrics.description: A clergyman openly seeking salary for gain's sake or displaying levity (jests from the pulpit) is felt to be objectionable; sacerdotal decorum demands dignity and restraint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even in secularized denominations there is a communal sense that bounds permissible indulgence for clergy are drawn closer than for laymen; community pressure enforces conformity or retirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gendered pattern: women's devoutness linked to vicarious leisure
rubrics_metrics.description: Middle-class women (and to a lesser degree lower artisan women) often constitute a vicarious leisure class whose economic position (domestic sphere) preserves habits of thought and conservatism that incline them to devout observances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sexual differentiation delegates much devotional life to women and children; adult males in the middle class are more exposed to industrial pressures and tend toward secularization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devout observances hinder economic efficiency and industrial adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Observances and the attendant habit of mind are obstructions to the effective organization of industry under modern circumstances and are, in proximate consequence, a curtailment of the community's economic efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both direct consumption in service of the divinity and the indirect reinforcement of status-oriented habits limit adaptation to modern quantitative, impersonal economic processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devoutness need not imply moral conformity
rubrics_metrics.description: A high degree of devout habit of mind need not carry with it strict observance of a code of morals (e.g., Decalogue or common law); criminal or dissolute classes may be devout in naïve or superstitious forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses focusing solely on economic/psychological aspects should neglect extra-economic moral distinctions unless investigating those specific questions.
